title: Informed Consent for LEP Patients in Obstetrics
summary: Build a safer obstetric informed consent workflow for patients with limited English proficiency across labor, anesthesia, and C-sections.
body_markdown:
###


The patient needs an understandable explanation of the proposed intervention, expected benefits, material risks, reasonable alternatives, and the option to decline. The patient must also have a chance to ask questions and make a voluntary decision.


###


Yes, when the system is built for healthcare, protects health information, provides appropriate quality controls, and fits hospital policy. The encounter type alone does not require a human interpreter.


###


No. If the patient can participate and there is time for a concise discussion, interpretation should begin immediately. If incapacity and immediate danger make consent impossible, follow applicable law and hospital policy, then explain the care after stabilization.


###


A family member should not be the default for an important medical decision. HHS guidance recognizes limited exceptions, including some patient-requested situations and temporary emergencies. Follow the organization’s language-access policy.


###


Document the language, interpretation method, intervention discussed, key risks and benefits, alternatives, patient questions, final decision, and how understanding was checked.
